= Debugging and Diagnosability
:description: Debug an Eventing Function with the JavaScript debugger, and use the system log and application logs to diagnose problems.
:page-topic-type: concept
:page-edition: Enterprise Edition

[abstract]
{description}

[#debugging-functions]
== Debugging Functions

The Eventing Service includes a JavaScript debugger that works with the Google Chrome DevTools debugger.
Use it to set breakpoints, step through code 1 line at a time, and inspect variable values.
The debugger uses a real mutation, so your Function runs under real conditions.

The default Eventing debug port is 9140.
To change it, see <<modifydebugport>>.

WARNING: Use the debugger only in development environments.
Debugging changes the order in which a Function processes mutations and can cause timing issues.

[#debugging-workflow]
=== How Debugging Works

A debug session works as follows:

* The Eventing Service takes 1 mutation from the Function's processing stream and sends it to the debugger.
The Function keeps processing all other mutations as usual.
* When a worker traps the mutation, it opens a temporary TCP port and generates a Chrome DevTools URL.
The URL contains a session cookie that controls the debug worker.
* Browser security prevents automatic opening of the URL, so you must copy and paste it into a new browser tab.
* After the trapped mutation finishes, the debugger does not trap any more mutations.
To debug another mutation, stop and restart the debugger.
* If you stop a debug session while the mutation is running, the Function might finish processing the mutation or cancel it.

[#enable-debugging]
=== Enable the Debugger

Enable the debugger only while you debug Functions.
When you finish, turn it off to keep your cluster secure.
While you have the debugger turned on, the code editor for a deployed Function shows a *Debug* control.

To enable the debugger:

. In the Couchbase Web Console, go to the *Eventing* page.
+
image::debugger_01_eventing_page.png["The Eventing page in the Couchbase Web Console",100%]
. Click btn:[Settings].
. In the *Eventing Settings* dialog, select *Enable debugger*.
+
image::debugger_02_eventing_settings.png["The Eventing Settings dialog with Enable debugger selected",350]
. Click btn:[Save].

[#debug-a-function]
=== Debug a Function

This example debugs the `case_2_enrich_ips` Function from xref:eventing-example-data-enrichment.adoc[Data Enrichment].
The Function listens to the `bulk.data.source` keyspace.

To start a debug session:

. On the *Eventing* page, click the name of the deployed Function to show its controls.
+
image::debugger_03_deployed_function.png["The controls for the deployed case_2_enrich_ips Function",100%]
. Click btn:[View JavaScript].
+
image::debugger_04_function_editor.png["The code editor showing the Function's JavaScript",100%]
. In the code editor, click btn:[Debug].
+
The debugger waits for the next mutation and shows the message `Waiting for mutation.`
+
image::debugger_05_debugger_waiting.png["The debugging dialog showing the Waiting for mutation message",100%]
+
Keep this browser tab open for the whole debug session.

If the Function receives a steady stream of mutations, you can skip the next procedure.

To create a mutation:

. In a new browser tab, open the Couchbase Web Console and go to the *Buckets* page.
. In the `bulk` bucket row, click *Scopes & Collections*.
. In the `data` scope row, click *Documents*.
. Select the `bulk` bucket, the `data` scope, and the `source` collection.
+
The collection has no documents.
+
image::debugger_06a_make_event.png["The Documents page for the bulk.data.source keyspace with no documents",100%]
. Click btn:[Add Document].
. In *ID*, enter `SampleDocument`.
. Replace the placeholder document body with the following JSON:
+
[source,json]
----
{
  "country": "AD",
  "ip_start": "5.62.60.1",
  "ip_end": "5.62.60.9"
}
----
+
image::debugger_06b_make_event.png["The Create New Document dialog with the SampleDocument ID and JSON body",100%]
. Click btn:[Save].
+
The new document creates a mutation in the Function's source keyspace.

To debug the mutation:

. Return to the tab that shows `Waiting for mutation.`
+
The dialog now shows a 1-time debugging URL.
+
image::debugger_07_debugger_have_url.png["The debugging dialog showing a 1-time debugging URL",100%]
. Click btn:[Copy].
. Open a new browser tab, then paste the URL into the address bar.
+
image::debugger_08_new_tab_paste_url.png["A new Chrome tab with the debugging URL in the address bar",100%]
. If the debugger does not show your Function's code, click *Step* 1 or 2 times.
+
image::debugger_09_chrome_step.png["The Chrome debugger with the Step control highlighted",100%]
. Click the line number for line 12 to set a breakpoint.
+
image::debugger_10_chrome_breakpoint.png["The Chrome debugger with a breakpoint on line 12",100%]
. Click *Resume* to run the Function until it reaches the breakpoint.
+
The Function runs as it would in production.
It runs any Data Service operations, {sqlpp} statements, and REST calls.
+
image::debugger_11_chrome_run_to_bp.png["The Chrome debugger with Resume highlighted",100%]
+
At the breakpoint, the debugger shows the current variable values:
+
image::debugger_12_chrome_run_at_bp.png["The Chrome debugger paused at line 12, showing variable values",100%]
. Click *Resume* again to finish running the Function.
. Return to the tab with the debugging dialog, then click btn:[Stop Debugging].

To debug another mutation, click btn:[Debug] again and repeat the process.
When you finish debugging, turn off the debugger in the *Eventing Settings* dialog.

[#debugging-problems]
=== Troubleshoot the Debugger

* The debug session ends if you close the tab with the debugging dialog or click btn:[Stop Debugging].
Keep that tab open, and create mutations in a different tab.
* Each debugging URL works for only 1 mutation.
To debug another mutation, click btn:[Stop Debugging], then click btn:[Debug] to get a new URL.
* If you connect to Couchbase Server through a NAT address, the debugging URL contains the internal address and does not work.
For more information, see <<debug-through-nat>>.
* Chrome sometimes changes the DevTools URL format.
If the URL does not open, see <<devtools-url-format>>.

[#debug-through-nat]
==== Debug Through a NAT Address

In this example, Couchbase Server runs at `192.168.3.150`, with port 8091 for the Web Console and port 9140 for the debugger.
The firewall maps the public address `4.71.116.187` to `192.168.3.150` for both ports.

To make the debugging URL use the public address, run the following command on the Couchbase Server node at `192.168.3.150`:

[source,sh]
----
curl -X PUT http://$CB_USERNAME:$CB_PASSWORD@localhost:8091/node/controller/setupAlternateAddresses/external \
    -d hostname=4.71.116.187 -d eventingDebug=9140
----

The debugging URL now uses the public address, so you do not need to edit it.

To remove the alternate address, run the following command on the same node:

[source,sh]
----
curl -X DELETE http://$CB_USERNAME:$CB_PASSWORD@localhost:8091/node/controller/setupAlternateAddresses/external \
    -d hostname=4.71.116.187 -d eventingDebug=9140
----

[#devtools-url-format]
==== DevTools URL Format

Depending on your Chrome version, you might need to edit the debugging URL after you paste it:

* Change the start of the URL from `chrome-devtools://` to `devtools://`.
* Change the end of the URL from `js_app.html` to `inspector.html`.

Chrome has used the following URL formats, from oldest to newest:

* `chrome-devtools://devtools/bundled/js_app.html`
* `devtools://devtools/bundled/js_app.html`
* `devtools://devtools/bundled/inspector.html`

// TODO(writer): confirm with Hiren (Eventing) which URL format the 8.5 debugger generates, and whether current Chrome versions still need these edits.

[#transpiler-source-map]
=== Transpiler and Source Map

A transpiler converts source code from 1 programming language into another.
Eventing Functions can contain {sqlpp} statements and `curl()` calls that standard JavaScript does not support.
Couchbase Server uses a transpiler to convert your Function's code into standard JavaScript that the JavaScript engine can compile.

The transpiler also generates a source map, which maps the transpiled code back to your original code.
The debugger detects the source map and shows your original code instead of the transpiled code.
When the debugger detects a source map, it shows a long comment at the end of the code.
The following example shows a truncated comment:

[source,text]
----
//# sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64,eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjozLCJzb3VyY2VzIjpb...
----

[#modifydebugport]
=== Change the Debug Port

The Eventing debug port, `eventing_debug_port`, defaults to 9140.
The Cluster Manager, `ns_server`, configures this port.
The port does not support access from outside the cluster, so use it only in development environments.

// TODO(writer): confirm with Hiren how this statement fits with the NAT setup in Debug Through a NAT Address, which exposes port 9140 publicly.

WARNING: Change port mappings only when you first set up a node.
Resetting the configuration deletes all data on the node.

To change the debug port on Linux:

. xref:install:install-intro.adoc[Install Couchbase Server].
. xref:install:startup-shutdown.adoc[Stop the Couchbase Server service].
. Add the new port to `/opt/couchbase/etc/couchbase/static_config`, in braces and followed by a period.
+
For example, to change the port from 9140 to 9444, add the following line:
+
[source,console]
----
{eventing_debug_port, 9444}.
----
. If you configured Couchbase Server before, delete `/opt/couchbase/var/lib/couchbase/config/config.dat` to remove the old configuration.
. xref:install:startup-shutdown.adoc[Start Couchbase Server].

For more information, see xref:install:install-ports.adoc#map-custom-ports[Custom Port Mapping].

[#logging-functions]
== Eventing Logs

The Eventing Service writes 2 types of logs:

* The <<system-log,system log>> records management and housekeeping information for the Eventing Service and all Functions.
* <<application-logs,Application logs>> record the messages that your Function's code writes with `log()`.
Each Function has its own application log.

[#system-log]
=== System Log

The Eventing Service writes its system log to `eventing.log`.
All Eventing Functions share this file.

The system log records management and supervision information for the Eventing Service.
It also records lifecycle and housekeeping information for each Function, based on the Function's *System Log Level* setting.
The system log does not record your Function's business logic, and your Function's code cannot write to it.
Couchbase Support uses the system log to troubleshoot problems.

The following table lists the default location of `eventing.log`:

.System Log Location by Platform
[cols="1,4"]
|====
| Platform | Location

| Linux
| `/opt/couchbase/var/lib/couchbase/logs/eventing.log`

| Windows
| `C:\Program Files\Couchbase\Server\var\lib\couchbase\logs\eventing.log`

| macOS
| `/Users/<user>/Library/Application\ Support/Couchbase/var/lib/couchbase/logs/eventing.log`
|====

The Windows path assumes the default installation location.

`eventing.log` contains redactable user data.
The `cbcollect_info` tool collects this file.
For more information about log rotation, see xref:manage:manage-logging/manage-logging.adoc#log-file-rotation[Log File Rotation].

The system log supports the following levels:

* Info, the default
* Error
* Warning
* Debug
* Trace

To change the level, use the *System Log Level* setting in the Function's settings.
The level controls how much detail the Function sends to the system log, and does not affect the Function's application log.
Do not change the level unless Couchbase Support asks you to.

image::debug_5_log_level.png["The System Log Level setting in the Function settings",484]

[#application-logs]
=== Application Logs

Application logs record the messages that your Function's code writes with `log()` statements.
Each Function has its own application log, named after the Function, such as `case_1_enrich_ips.log`.
Application logs have no log level.
Use them to develop and debug your Function's business logic.

To view a Function's application log in the Web Console or with the REST API, you need the appropriate RBAC privileges.
Users with the Full Admin or Eventing Full Admin role can view the application log of any Function.
For more information, see xref:eventing-rbac.adoc[Eventing Role-Based Access Control].

To view the application log of a deployed Function, go to the *Eventing* page and click *Log* for the Function.
You can also read the log file on each Eventing node with commands such as `cat`, `tail`, or `tail -F`.

The following Function writes the document, the result of a `curl()` call, and any error to its application log:

[source,javascript]
----
function OnUpdate(doc, meta) {
    log('document', doc);
    try {
        var response = curl(
            'http://localhost:3000/notify',
            {method : 'POST', data : doc}
        );
        log('curl', response);
    } catch (e) {
        log('error', e);
    }
}
----

[#log-with-try-catch]
==== Log Errors with Try-Catch Blocks

To make your Function easier to debug, use `log()` statements with `try`/`catch` blocks.

The following Function processes 1 document from the `travel-sample` bucket, but uses an undefined variable `a` without a `try`/`catch` block:

[source,javascript]
----
function OnUpdate(doc, meta) {
    if (meta.id != "airport_1255") return
    log('id', meta.id);
    // The undefined variable 'a' stops processing.
    // View JavaScript shows an error indicator [X] on this line,
    // and the Eventing statistics count the mutation as a failure.
    if (a == 1) {
        log('a is 1')
    }
    // never reached
    log('complete')
}
----

The Function writes only the first of its 3 log messages, then stops.
The statistics count the mutation as failed:

[source,text]
----
2020-02-09T07:12:17.936-08:00 [INFO] "id" "airport_1255"
----

For a deployed Function, click btn:[View JavaScript] to see an error indicator, *[X]*, on the line that failed.
Point to the indicator for more information.

With a `try`/`catch` block, the log shows the cause of the failure.
The Function also counts the mutation as processed instead of failed, because the code catches and handles the error:

[source,javascript]
----
function OnUpdate(doc, meta) {
    if (meta.id != "airport_1255") return
    log('id', meta.id);
    try {
        if (a == 1) {
            log('a is 1')
        }
    } catch (e) {
        log('error', e);
    }
    log('complete')
}
----

The application log now shows the exact error:

[source,text]
----
2020-02-09T07:12:17.936-08:00 [INFO] "id" "airport_1255"
2020-02-09T07:12:17.936-08:00 [INFO] "error" "ReferenceError: a is not defined"
2020-02-09T07:12:17.936-08:00 [INFO] "complete"
----

[#exception-summaries]
==== Exception Summaries

Application logs also record a summary of low-level issues and exceptions once a minute for each worker.
For example, if 1 million documents throw the same exception, each worker logs 1 summary message with the line number and a count.

When the following Function runs on the `travel-sample._default._default` keyspace, 31,591 mutations fail:

[source,javascript]
----
function OnUpdate(doc, meta) {
    if (a == 1) {
        // never reached
        log('a is 1')
    }
    // never reached
    log('complete')
}
----

The application log summarizes the failures in 1 line for each worker:

[source,text]
----
2021-07-19T15:35:44.895-07:00 [INFO] {"count":31591,"exception":"\"ReferenceError: a is not defined\"","file":"test_summary.js","line":2,"since":"2021-07-19T15:35:44","srcLine":"if (a == 1) {","stack":"ReferenceError: a is not defined\n    at OnUpdate (test_summary.js:3:5)"}
----

Summaries keep the application log small when a Function has a low-level issue, or a syntax error that appears only at deploy time.

[#app-log-files]
==== Application Log Files and Rotation

Each Eventing node writes its own application log file for each Function.
Each file contains only the mutations that the node processed.

NOTE: The `cbcollect_info` tool does not collect application log files.

The following table lists the default directory for application log files:

.Application Log Location by Platform
[cols="1,4"]
|====
| Platform | Location

| Linux
| `/opt/couchbase/var/lib/couchbase/data/@eventing/`

| Windows
| `C:\Program Files\Couchbase\Server\var\lib\couchbase\data\@eventing\`

| macOS
| `/Users/<user>/Library/Application\ Support/Couchbase/var/lib/couchbase/data/@eventing/`
|====

The Windows path assumes the default installation location.
If you chose a custom Indexes path during cluster setup, application logs are in the `@eventing` folder under that path.

By default, each application log file can grow to 40 MB, and Eventing keeps 10 files.
To change these limits, set `app_log_max_size` in bytes and `app_log_max_files` in the Function settings with the REST API.
When you call the settings endpoint, you must always include `deployment_status` and `processing_status`.
For more information, see xref:eventing-rest-api:index.adoc#settings_schema[Eventing REST API].

The following example keeps 10 log files of about 10 MB each.

Sample URL: `\http://192.168.1.5:8091/_p/event/api/v1/functions/<function_name>/settings`

Sample payload:

[source,json]
----
{
  "settings": {
    "deployment_status": false,
    "processing_status": false,
    "app_log_max_files": 10,
    "app_log_max_size": 10485760
  }
}
----

When the active log file reaches the size limit, Eventing renames it and starts a new active file.
For example, when `case_1_enrich_ips.log` reaches 10 MB, Eventing renames it to `case_1_enrich_ips.log.1` and creates a new `case_1_enrich_ips.log`.
With `app_log_max_files` set to 10, Eventing keeps the active file and 9 earlier files, and deletes the oldest file when it creates a new file.

[#log-redaction]
== Log Redaction

Log redaction removes sensitive data from logs, such as:

* Personally identifiable information (PII)
* Hostnames
* Internal asset information
* Credit card details
Organizations use log redaction to meet legal compliance and security requirements.

NOTE: Log redaction applies only to the system log, not to application logs.

For more information, see xref:manage:manage-logging/manage-logging.adoc#understanding_redaction[Understanding Redaction].
